newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end up after T-bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end up after T-bill auction.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended higher on Wednesday after coming off morning lows on a T-bill auction that dealers called unsuccessful.
Yields initially fell on strong foreign markets and relief after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan'ss speech to the U.S. Senate painted a fairly positive picture of the economy.
But the market changed with a T-bill auction at 1150 GMT.
The auction of 12 month bills was marginally oversubscribed and dealers said the top rate, 3.819 percent, was very high.
"The T-bill auction was mediocre and made the T-bill rates climbed several basis points," one dealer said.
Sweden Statistics figures showed industrial production rose by 3.1 percent in November, the biggest volume produced 1911 when monitoring began. It did not affect the market.
The Riksbank meeting was the focus for Thursday, dealers said. It starts at 0745 GMT.
Since the Riksbank did not cut the repo rate on Tuesday there were some expectations of a cut on Thursday but a Reuter survey found the market consensus was for the Riksbank to leave rates unchanged.
